Confirmed — the real, already-wired `StoreKitManager` (`purchaseAuraPlus`/`restorePurchases`/`startEntitlementListener`) already exists and is exactly what Codex B's new `StoreManager.swift` reinvents.

- **Codex B's `Services/Purchases/StoreManager.swift` is a straight duplicate of the already-real, already-integrated `Services/StoreKit/StoreKitManager.swift`** (verified: same three methods exist there today, live in `SettingsScreen.swift`). This is precisely the "never a parallel StoreKit implementation" pattern this project's decision log has flagged before for the day-state/streak duplication — same risk, new subsystem.
- **`UI/Settings/PurchaseFlowView.swift` reuses the literal identifier `"settings.purchaseButton"`** on a second, never-mounted button — nothing in the view hierarchy presents `PurchaseFlowView`, so it's dead code, but if it ever got wired in, two controls sharing one accessibilityIdentifier is a new crawl-ambiguity risk on top of being redundant with the real purchase button already in `SettingsScreen.swift`.
- **`PurchaseSheetView` wraps `SKPaymentQueueViewController`** — that's not a real StoreKit/UIKit type (StoreKit 1 has no such view controller); this won't compile once it's actually in the target.
- **`WatermarkOverlay.swift`/`ImageExporter.swift`/`MetadataScrubber.swift` duplicate work `ExportPipeline.swift` already does for real** — watermark compositing and EXIF/metadata stripping are already implemented there (by design, inside the renderer/export path, never a SwiftUI-view overlay per `ExportPipeline`'s own doc comments). A second, view-based watermark/export path is a parallel implementation, not an extension of the existing one.
- **`Configuration/StoreKitTestConfig.storekit` duplicates the already-existing, already-scheme-wired `Aura.storekit`** at the repo root (see `project.yml`'s `storeKitConfiguration: Aura.storekit`) — nothing points to this new file.
- **None of these five new files will even compile yet** — they'd hit the exact same stale-`project.pbxproj` bug Claude B and I both diagnosed last round (new files aren't in the target until `xcodegen generate` runs). Adding more duplicate-symbol files on top of an already-broken build compounds the diagnosis rather than fixing it.

My lane (`TodayScreen.swift`/`RootTabView.swift`) is unaffected by any of this — nothing to change there this round. **For the integrator:** don't merge any of Codex B's five new files as-is; the real ask (regenerate `Aura.xcodeproj` via `xcodegen generate` to pick up last round's `BootstrapRecipeBuilder`) is still the actual, minimal fix outstanding.
